title: Visualizing Quantum Mechanics: 1D Box
text:
The “Particle in a 1D Box” is usually the very first problem encountered in quantum mechanics. It describes a particle free to move in a small space surrounded by impenetrable barriers.
The probability of finding the particle at a specific position \(x\) is given by the square of its wave function:
\[|\psi_n(x)|^2 = \frac{2}{L} \sin^2\left(\frac{n \pi x}{L}\right)\]
Use the slider below to change the principal quantum number (\(n\)) and observe how the probability density shifts. Notice that as \(n\) increases, the number of “nodes” (places where the probability is zero) also increases!

title: Wordle Solver
text:
View the Source Code on GitHub
Wordle is essentially a game of managing uncertainty. While humans play it using intuition and vocabulary, a computer can play it by mathematically minimizing the search space.

title: Wordle Solver
text:
Version 1.0: The Greedy Approach (Current)
The initial build of this solver relies on a procedural, “greedy” algorithm. It evaluates a list of possible answers and selects the word that maximizes the immediate number of “Green” and “Yellow” hits.
While somewhat effective at finding an answer within 6 guesses, a purely greedy algorithm often falls into traps as it optimizes for the current turn rather than setting up the optimal board state for the next turn.

title: Wordle Solver
text:
The Roadmap: Future Implementations
I have a few plans to refine the solver:

Run simulations to get an average of how many time the greedy approach wins
Create a manual mode which gives players the next best guesses
Transitioning the codebase into a WordleSolver class to allow for 10,000+ game and run simulations to benchmark algorithmic efficiency.
Implementing a strict filtering mechanism to dynamically shrink the possible word list after every guess.
Fixing edge-case bugs surrounding words with duplicate letters.
Upgrading the guessing logic from a greedy approach to one that uses information theory. The algorithm will calculate the expected information gain (in bits) for every possible word, selecting the guess that mathematically eliminates the largest portion of the remaining search space.
